content: 1. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of levofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, separate the doses by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. 2. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of levoketoconazole by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction also applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug, and separate administration by 2 hours if necessary. Monitor closely. 3. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of lisdexamfetamine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of lisinopril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Mannitol decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. This is considered a minor interaction with unknown clinical significance. Monitor closely. 6. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of memantine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Aluminum hydroxide interacts with mesalamine through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. This is a minor interaction with unknown significance. Salicylate levels may increase at moderate doses and decrease at high doses due to increased renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. 8. Mestranol decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide through a mechanism involving magnesium shifting from blood to tissue storage. This is a minor interaction with unknown significance. Monitor closely. 9. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of methscopolamine by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Methyclothiazide decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. This is a minor interaction with unknown significance. Monitor closely. 11. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of methylphenidate by enhancing GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. For extended-release methylphenidate capsules (e.g., Ritalin LA), co-administration with antacids or acid suppressants may alter drug release. Consider separating administration of the antacid and methylphenidate. 12. Metolazone decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. This is a minor interaction with unknown significance. Monitor closely. 13. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of metoprolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 14. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of mexiletine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels of minocycline by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 16. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of moexipril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels of moxifloxacin by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 18. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of mycophenolate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of nadolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 20. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of nebivolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 21. Neomycin reduces the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. This is a minor interaction with unknown significance. Monitor closely. 22. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of neratinib by increasing gastric pH. Separate administration by 3 hours and monitor closely. 23. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of nilotinib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid this interaction by administering antacids 2 hours before or after nilotinib. 24. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of nimodipine by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of nisoldipine by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of nitrendipine by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of nitrofurantoin by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels of nitrofurantoin by inhibiting GI absorption. This is a minor interaction with unknown significance. Monitor closely. 29. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels of ofloxacin by inhibiting GI absorption. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 30. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of omadacycline by inhibiting GI absorption. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair absorption of tetracyclines, reducing efficacy. Separate dosing of tetracyclines from these products. 31. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels of oxytetracycline by inhibiting GI absorption. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 32. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of pamidronate by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 33. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the effects of pancrelipase through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Paromomycin reduces the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. This is a minor interaction with unknown significance. Monitor closely. 35. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of pazopanib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration with drugs that raise gastric pH. Short-acting antacids may be used instead of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) or H2 antagonists, but separate administration by several hours. 36. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of penbutolol by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 37. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels of penicillamine by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 38. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of perindopril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of pexidartinib by inhibiting GI absorption. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Separate administration by 2 hours before or after taking a locally-acting antacid. 40. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of pindolol by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 41. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of polysaccharide iron by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels of ponatinib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of posaconazole by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the effects of potassium phosphates (IV) by cation binding in the GI tract. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of propranolol by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 46. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of pseudoephedrine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of quinapril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of quinidine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of raltegavir by cation binding in the GI tract. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 50. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of ramipril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of rifampin by reducing absorption. Administer rifampin at least 1 hour before antacids. 52. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of rilpivirine by increasing gastric pH. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 53. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels of riociguat by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by at least 1 hour and monitor closely. 54. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of risedronate by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 55. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of rosuvastatin by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 56. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels of tetracycline by inhibiting GI absorption. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 57. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of tiludronate by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 58. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of timolol by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 59. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels of zoledronic acid by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 60. Prolonged antacid therapy may result in hypophosphatemia due to the formation of insoluble phosphate complexes, leading to decreased phosphate absorption in the GI tract. Severe hypophosphatemia may cause anorexia, malaise, muscle weakness, and osteomalacia. 61. Prolonged therapy may result in aluminum intoxication or hypermagnesemia, particularly in patients with renal impairment. Aluminum intoxication may lead to osteomalacia or dialysis encephalopathy. 62. Pregnancy Category C: Use caution during pregnancy and lactation, as excretion in breast milk is unknown.
